blocks.orig: Tanzania weather differs from region to region – but there is always a great time to travel in Tanzania! Weather in the coastal areas is the hottest and most humid, while the North and highlands of Tanzania are cooler because of altitude. The temperatures vary between 22°C and 31 °C throughout the year. During the night, the temperature in Tanzania drops to between 10°C and 22°C. The beaches of Zanzibar have a distinctively tropical climate since it is located close to the Equator.
blocks.html: The weather in Tanzania varies from one region to the next – but there is always a good moment to travel somewhere in the country! Along the coast it is hottest and most humid, while the north and the highlands stay cooler thanks to their altitude. Over the year, temperatures range between 22°C and 31 °C. At night they fall to somewhere between 10°C and 22°C. Because Zanzibar lies close to the Equator, its beaches have a distinctly tropical climate.

blocks.orig: Tanzania has two seasons yearly: the wet and the dry season. The wet season (also called the rainy season) runs from the end of October right through to December, and then again from the end of March to the beginning of June. They are referred to as the ‘short-’ and ‘long rains’. These tropical rains mostly start late afternoon and continue all night till early morning. The rains of Africa are famous worldwide and are a soothing, enchanting sight to behold during a trip to Tanzania!
blocks.html: Each year Tanzania has two seasons: a wet one and a dry one. The wet season (or rainy season) lasts from the end of October through to December, and returns from the end of March until early June. These periods are known as the ‘short’ and the ‘long rains’. The tropical showers usually begin in the late afternoon and carry on through the night into the early morning. The rains of Africa are famous around the world, and watching them during a trip to Tanzania is a calming, enchanting experience!

blocks.orig: Can I go on safari during the rainy season?
blocks.html: Is a safari possible in the rainy season?

blocks.orig: Did you know that National Geographic, Discovery and other major media companies choose the rainy season to shoot their wildlife documentaries in Tanzania? Tanzania weather is fantastic all year round and though heavy rains persist most afternoons in the rainy season, the natural environment comes to life. Nature is colourful, the grass is lush and green, beautiful flowers grow, animals find plenty of food, temperatures are nice and cool and, better yet, the main highlights of Tanzania are far less crowded with tourists.
blocks.html: Were you aware that National Geographic, Discovery and other big media companies pick the rainy season to film their wildlife documentaries in Tanzania? The weather here is wonderful throughout the year, and although heavy showers fall most afternoons in the rainy season, this is when nature truly comes alive. Everything is colourful, the grass is lush and green, flowers bloom, animals have food in abundance, temperatures are pleasantly cool and, best of all, the main highlights of Tanzania see far fewer tourists.

blocks.orig: Another benefit of travelling in rainy reason is the lower costs of safaris and accommodation during this low season. The disadvantages of travel during the wet season are that some accommodations are closed and the (sometimes) poor road conditions. Fortunately, this mainly concerns the roads in the national parks in South Tanzania.
blocks.html: A further advantage of visiting in the rainy season is that safaris and accommodation cost less during this low season. The drawbacks are that some accommodations close and that road conditions can (occasionally) be poor. Luckily, this mostly applies to the roads in the national parks of South Tanzania.

blocks.orig: For those travelling to Tanzania during the rainy season, the following national parks are open and ready for your visit. Serengeti, Ngorongoro Crater, Tarangire, Lake Manyara, Lake Natron and Arusha National Park. The national parks of Tanzania that are better avoided during the wet season include Nyerere, Ruaha, Mikumi & Udzungwa. So if any of the latter destinations are on your must-do list in Tanzania, be sure to head out in dry season.
blocks.html: If you travel to Tanzania in the rainy season, these national parks remain open and ready to welcome you: Serengeti, Ngorongoro Crater, Tarangire, Lake Manyara, Lake Natron and Arusha National Park. The parks that are best left for another time during the wet season are Nyerere, Ruaha, Mikumi & Udzungwa. So if one of those destinations is high on your list for Tanzania, make sure you go in the dry season.

blocks.orig: How does Tanzania weather affect wildlife?
blocks.html: What does the weather in Tanzania mean for the wildlife?

blocks.orig: The rain makes for a lush landscape with a high concentration of animals. This means plenty of opportunities to spot wildlife at their finest – and happiest! During the rainy seasons, animals are more active which makes for a fantastic safari experience. With an abundance of food and fresh water, animals roam in their thousands. The rain also protects the animals from the harsh heat of the sun.
blocks.html: The rain produces a lush landscape with a high concentration of animals, which gives you plenty of chances to see wildlife at its finest – and happiest! In the rainy seasons the animals are more active, and that makes for a wonderful safari. With food and fresh water everywhere, they roam in their thousands. The rain also shields them from the fierce heat of the sun.

blocks.orig: Many of our safari guests say that the rainy season offers a more intimate safari experience. For bird lovers, the rainy season is a fantastic time of year to visit Tanzania as lots of migratory birds arrive.
blocks.html: A lot of our safari guests tell us the rainy season gives a more intimate safari. If you love birds, it is a fantastic time of year to come to Tanzania, as large numbers of migratory birds arrive.
